headline: Break the circle by excluding an endpoint
statement: Houses form a circle, so the first and last are adjacent. Choose no adjacent houses and maximize the total money.
intuition: Any legal choice omits at least one of the two endpoints. Solve the line excluding the last house and the line excluding the first house, then take the larger optimum. A single house is a separate case because it can be taken.
approach: Return the only amount for a singleton.
Run the linear robber recurrence on indices 0 through n-2.
Run it again on indices 1 through n-1.
correctness: Every valid circular selection belongs to at least one endpoint-excluded line because it cannot contain both endpoints. Conversely, a nonadjacent selection in either line is circularly legal. Therefore the maximum of their optima is precisely the circular optimum.
bruteForce: Enumerate all subsets and reject adjacent selected houses, including the endpoint pair. This takes exponential time.

complexity.explanation: Two linear scans use index ranges rather than copied slices.

pitfalls: The first and last houses cannot both be selected.
Do not simply subtract the smaller endpoint from a linear optimum.
